chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from al-Washshāʾ, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who fell upon another man from the top of a house, and one of the two died. He said: “There is nothing upon the upper one, and there is nothing upon the lower one.”

key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَى الْأَعْلَى شَيْءٌ: no liability is upon the one above
key_terms.مِنْ فَوْقِ الْبَيْتِ: from the top of the house
key_terms.وَلَا عَلَى الْأَسْفَلِ شَيْءٌ: and no liability is upon the one below

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one man falls from a roof onto another man and one of them dies?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a fatal accidental fall in which one man falls upon another from the top of a house and one of them dies. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام rules that neither the upper one nor the lower one bears liability in this case, indicating the absence of diyyah or legal responsibility under these circumstances.
